title: An image encryption algorithm based on a novel hyperchaotic Henon sine map
authors: Madhu Sharma; Ranjeet Kumar Ranjan; Vishal Bharti
key_initialisation: 256-bit key split into eight 32-bit words; XOR pairs -> 16 subkeys mapped (mod 1) to ICs and parameters of two 2D-HSM instances
sequence_generation: two chaotic matrices S1, S2 of image size (8-bit elements)
permutation: two rounds of confusion with roles of S1/S2 swapped
diffusion: diffusion inside each round plus an embedded diffusion between rounds
decryption: reverse order of the encryption steps
evaluation_metrics: histogram, correlation, key sensitivity, NPCR/UACI, local Shannon entropy, speed
attack_models: key sensitivity, differential (NPCR/UACI); no executed KPA/CPA attack
reported_strengths: large nominal key space (2^256); 1-pixel random border makes ciphertexts differ per run
identified_limitations: security argued from statistics; random border adds randomness without a defined nonce model
relation_to_this_project: reference workflow only; its key mapping, border, round structure and diffusion are explicitly NOT reused

title: A New Sine-Ikeda Modulated Chaotic Key for Cybersecurity
authors: S. Hanis
map_or_system: Sine-Ikeda modulated map: Ikeda map plus additive l*sin(pi*x_n), l*sin(pi*y_n)
key_initialisation: seed ICs fixed in the paper (x0=1.8888887, y0=0.9234567); harmonic means of generated sequences become new seeds; control parameters changed each iteration
sequence_generation: chaotic sequences used directly as keys
permutation: not part of the paper (key generator only)
evaluation_metrics: bifurcation, Lyapunov exponent, cycle length, ApEn, NIST SP 800-22 (100 x 10^6 bits, alpha 0.001)
identified_limitations: no encryption scheme; additive sine modulation differs from ISC's Ikeda -> sin -> T2 composition
relation_to_this_project: closest Ikeda+sine map; ISC differs structurally (composition, Chebyshev T2 stage)
